claim: Islands close in NE monsoon (~mid-Oct–Feb), reopen early March; April–June best for calm seas and fewer crowds; Jul–Sep busiest.
quote: Most tourist activity comes to a standstill from October to March... November is particularly severe and should be avoided at all costs... generally the islands open up in early March each year.

claim: April to June recommended to balance good weather with avoiding crowds and monsoon.
quote: the best time to visit is between April and June, when you'll avoid the crowds and avoid the monsoon.

claim: April, May and June give calm, pool-like seas and peak visibility with fewer crowds and possible accommodation discounts.
quote: sea conditions during this period are extremely calm, similar to a swimming pool, perfect for snorkeling and island activities.

claim: Ferry service to the Perhentians typically resumes in late February ahead of the March season opening.
quote: Perhentian Islands typically resume ferry service in late February.

claim: Reference list of Malaysia 2026 federal and state public holidays.
quote: Public Holidays 2026 - Calendar Malaysia

claim: Hari Raya Puasa (Aidilfitri) 2026 falls 21 March in Malaysia.
quote: Hari Raya Puasa 2026 in Malaysia

claim: Terengganu declared Thursday 19 March 2026 a state public holiday for Aidilfitri and kept 23 March as gazetted holiday.
quote: Terengganu declares March 19 a public holiday for Aidilfitri

claim: Hari Raya Aidilfitri 2026 fell Sat 21 and Sun 22 March, with a 4-day national long weekend Fri 20–Mon 23 March.
quote: Hari Raya Aidilfitri 2026 fell on Saturday 21 March (Day 1) and Sunday 22 March (Day 2).

claim: Chinese New Year 2026 is Tue 17 February; Terengganu and Kelantan do not observe the second day (18 Feb).
quote: the second day of the celebration (18 February 2026), most of the states will have a public holiday except Kelantan and Terengganu.

claim: Hari Raya Aidiladha (Haji) 2026 is 27–28 May; Terengganu also observes Hari Arafah on 26 May.
quote: Hari Raya Aidiladha in Malaysia will fall on 27 & 28 May 2026.

claim: Eid al-Adha 2026 in Malaysia falls 27 May, creating a long weekend in several states.
quote: Eid Al Adha in Malaysia 2026: Date, Public Holiday & Celebrations

claim: Kampung Pasir Hantu is the only settlement, 2000+ villagers, plain unpainted wooden houses; Besar has no village.
quote: Kampung Pasir Hantu which is resided with more than 2000 villagers and completed with basic facilities... houses... remain in the original plain wooden colour except police station, assembly hall and school.

claim: Kampung Pasir Hantu covers 9.87 hectares on Perhentian Kecil and has a mosque among its facilities.
quote: Kampung Pasir Hantu is a settlement area on Pulau Perhentian Kecil with an area of 9.87 hectares. Among the facilities found in this area is a mosque.

claim: About 80% of Perhentian's ~1,300 residents work in tourism; the rest in public sector and retail.
quote: The total population of Pulau Perhentian is about 1,300 people with almost 80% are involved in tourism sector, 20% in public sector and retail traders.

claim: Village homestays in Kampung Pasir Hantu sit next to the mosque, which offers free tours.
quote: located in the local fishing village and next to the mosque (which offers really great free tours).

claim: Muslim-owned restaurants can't sell alcohol; BYO permitted in many dry restaurants; some resorts (Coral View) ask no alcohol; conservation/sunscreen etiquette; monsoon closure.
quote: Muslim-owned restaurants can't sell any... bringing your own is also permitted in most otherwise dry restaurants... At Coral View Resort... alcohol is not served and you are asked to not bring your own.

claim: Bars on Long Beach serve at night, alcohol at resorts; travellers advise buying on mainland; villages stricter.
quote: There are a few bars serving alcohol on Long Beach at night... Just stay away from the villages though, they may be a little strict over there.

claim: Bikinis allowed on Perhentian beaches but cover up off the sand; swimwear in towns/shops is disrespectful.
quote: Bikinis are allowed on the beaches of the Perhentian Islands, but you should cover up... Wearing swimwear in town centers, shops, or restaurants is considered culturally disrespectful.

claim: Terengganu pushing Syariah-compliant dress code enforcement aimed mainly at Muslim tourists, naming Redang and Perhentian islands.
quote: the focus is on popular tourist destinations like Redang and Perhentian islands... targets foreign Muslim tourists.

claim: Non-Muslim tourists are not bound by Terengganu's clothing etiquette but should respect local Malay culture.
quote: Non-Muslim tourists not tied to clothing etiquette in Terengganu

claim: Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah observe a Friday–Saturday weekend with a Sunday–Thursday working week, aligned to Friday Islamic observance.
quote: Kelantan and Terengganu observe a Friday–Saturday weekend... working days are from Sundays to Thursdays.

claim: During Ramadan on Kecil, food places run normally until the sunset iftar, with a wait while fasting staff eat; resorts well-stocked.
quote: food places are not affected too much during Ramadan, with normal service until sunset when the fasting is broken, though there is a long wait while staff eat.

claim: Many island staff fast during Ramadan, eating after nightfall and before sunrise.
quote: Many of the staff on the islands fast during Ramadan and often raid the kitchen during nightfall and ahead of sunrise.

claim: Masjid Ar Rahman is the village mosque on Perhentian Kecil overlooking the ocean.
quote: Masjid A R Rahman Pulau Perhentian | Attractions - Lonely Planet

claim: The Perhentian Island mosque is busy at Friday prayers and gives the adhan at the five daily prayer times.
quote: the mosque is busy during Friday prayers... gives out beautiful Adhan (prayer call) recitations during the 5 Islamic prayer times.

claim: Perhentian Turtle Project conserves endangered green and critically endangered hawksbill turtles via research, monitoring and citizen science.
quote: Green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas) – Endangered... Hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata) – Critically Endangered.

claim: Perhentian Turtle Project was established in 2015 under Fuze Ecoteer in the Perhentian Islands Marine Park, running hatchery and patrol work.
quote: The Perhentian Turtle Project (PTP) was officially established in 2015 as a sea turtle research and conservation initiative under Fuze Ecoteer Outdoor Adventures.

claim: Bubbles Turtle Conservation returned to begin the 2026 nesting season on 11 March 2026.
quote: On the afternoon of 11th March 2026, the team at Bubbles Turtle Conservation returned to the Perhentian Islands to begin preparing for the 2026 turtle nesting season.

claim: The boat fare excludes the Marine Park fee, paid at the jetty; Malaysia is multi-cultural so check holiday calendars.
quote: The boat fare does not include the Marine Park fee, which you can pay at a dedicated counter in the jetty terminal.

claim: Marine Park Conservation Charge is RM30 for foreign adults and RM5 for locals, funding the marine-park trust fund.
quote: Proceeds from the fees will be credited into the Marine Park and Marine Reserve Trust Fund.

claim: The Marine Park conservation ticket (RM30 foreigners) must be paid at the Kuala Besut jetty counter before boarding.
quote: This ticket is paid at Marine Park counter in the Kuala Besut Jetty, so pay this BEFORE you get on the boat.

claim: Pulau Duyong boat-makers are world famous for hand-crafting wooden boats without blueprints or nails.
quote: Using no blue prints and no nails, the boat makers of Pulau Duyong are world famous for hand-crafting boats.

claim: The bangau figurehead supports the sail and was believed to hold a protective spirit; owners hold blessing ceremonies.
quote: it was also believed that a motif of the bangau had a spirit and that it would keep them safe on their voyages.

claim: Traditional Terengganu boat-building is an inherited heritage now threatened by declining youth interest and demand.
quote: Terengganu... menyimpan tradisi pembuatan bot yang diwarisi turun-temurun.

claim: Terengganu crafts include batik, songket, rattan, wood carving, wau and the keris, a Nusantara symbol of identity and status.
quote: Keris is the most recognised symbol of the Nusantara, seen as a symbol of identity, grandeur and supremacy.

claim: Terengganu's songket weavers are considered the country's best; the craft is endangered but seeing a fashion-led revival.
quote: The songket is one of Terengganu's top products whose weavers are considered to be the best in the country.

claim: Kuala Besut is a coastal gateway town with a market of batik, woven mats and handicrafts plus traditional Terengganu food.
quote: Kuala Besut Market features handicrafts, batik, woven mats, and fresh seafood.

claim: Kuala Besut offers Bukit Keluang hiking views and local culture beyond its role as the ferry port.
quote: Bukit Keluang Hill: A hiking destination offering panoramic views of the coastline.

claim: The Crystal Mosque, built of steel and glass, sits within Taman Tamadun Islam (Islamic Civilisation Park) in Kuala Terengganu.
quote: Crystal Mosque - Taman Tamadun Islam

claim: Taman Tamadun Islam features walk-around scale models of Islamic monuments (incl. enterable Dome of the Rock); open Mon–Thu 10–19, Fri–Sun 9–19.
quote: Monday-Thursday: 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM; Friday-Sunday: 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

claim: Taman Tamadun Islam admission is about RM21.20 adult and RM15.90 child/senior; mosque entry free.
quote: For adults, the entrance is RM21.20 (US$4.90) and for a child or senior citizen it is RM15.90 (US$3.65).

claim: Masjid Tengku Tengah Zaharah (Floating Mosque), completed 1994, appears to float on a lagoon ~4 km from Kuala Terengganu centre.
quote: Since its completion in 1994, it has become one of the most photographed and visited sites in the state.

claim: The Tengku Tengah Zaharah Mosque is Malaysia's first floating mosque.
quote: Tengku Tengah Zaharah Mosque - Wikipedia

claim: Terengganu State Museum is the biggest museum complex in Southeast Asia, with maritime museum and traditional houses; entry RM5/RM3.
quote: The Terengganu State Museum is the biggest museum complex in South-east Asia with four main blocks besides having a maritime museum and five traditional houses.

claim: Terengganu State Museum opening hours are 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.
quote: The museum's operating hours are 9:00 am - 5:00 pm.

claim: Kuala Terengganu Chinatown (Kampung Cina) has 19th-C shophouses, a dragon arch and street art; lively at CNY, Mooncake and Dragon Boat festivals.
quote: Kampung Cina, or Chinatown, is a compact heritage district filled with colorful 19th century shophouses, temples, and street art.

claim: Ho Ann Kiong, built 1801 by Hokkien settlers, is Kuala Terengganu's oldest Taoist temple; Turtle Alley promotes turtle conservation.
quote: Built in 1801 by early Hokkien settlers, Ho Ann Kiong Temple is the oldest Taoist temple in Kuala Terengganu.

claim: Pasar Payang has produce/seafood downstairs and batik/songket upstairs, operates ~07:30–18:00, and is cash-only.
quote: fresh produce, seafood, and local snacks downstairs, and batik, songket, and household goods upstairs. The market operates from 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM, and transactions are primarily done in cash.
